# EE4213 Fall 2026 project delivery

Use this course-specific checklist to check completeness and consistency. These requirements apply to the EE4213 Fall 2026 group project only; confirm the latest course instructions before reusing them in another term.

## Keep the project coherent

- Present the project context and research goal, final primary and related secondary personas, problem statements, and how the team synthesized individual findings.
- Explain the relationship between personas and problems through a shared service, ecosystem, or workflow. Structure multiple problem statements hierarchically.
- Define prototype boundaries and focus the presentation on one to three impactful features. Skip account registration, login, and password recovery unless those flows provide substantial value to the solution.
- Explain which individual-prototype elements were included, adjusted, reworked, deferred, or excluded, and justify the decisions with research, user needs, and constraints.
- If AI is included, explain the interaction pattern, human-oversight boundary, and lifecycle considerations. A well-reasoned decision not to use AI is acceptable.

## Deliverables

- **Presentation:** approximately 15–25 slides, no more than 12 minutes. Communicate the evidence and decisions concisely; demonstrate the primary end-to-end workflow and any connected secondary workflow.
- **Functional prototype:** a working high-fidelity prototype or application that reflects user feedback and demonstrates selected stories. For software, provide a cloud-hosted prototype or application, code or a final-prototype link, and a demonstration video hosted on YouTube. Keep the video consistent with the presented deliverable.
- **Written report:** cover project context and research goal; personas and problem hierarchy; synthesis of individual work; solution scope and design rationale; validation method, findings, and before/after changes; backlog and sprint planning; retrospective; and AI collaboration assessment.
- **Validation appendix:** include the study plan and questions, documentation and recordings for every usability session, and other supporting material. Secure participants' consent before recording.
- **Backlog:** include at least two themes, three epics per theme, and four user stories per epic. Assign story points, provide acceptance criteria for selected stories, explain prioritization, and trace stories to evidence or design decisions. For AI-assisted stories, document what was accepted, changed, rejected, or deferred and why.
- **Sprint planning:** define goals for one-week sprints, select stories that can be completed within each sprint, and explain the prioritization method and trade-offs.
- **Conclusion:** include a sprint retrospective (successes, underlying challenges, improvements/skills gaps, next actions) and an AI collaboration reflection (strengths, limitations, verification, accepted/edited/rejected output, and lessons for next time).

## Final consistency check

Verify that the report, slides, prototype, selected user stories, and validation evidence all describe the same scope and user workflows. Show a clear chain from user evidence to problem, design decision, tested change, and implemented prototype behavior. Do not claim validation, functionality, or AI behavior that the evidence and prototype do not demonstrate.

The supplied Fall 2026 brief lists a submission deadline of 17 November 2026 at 12:00 noon. Check the current course page for any update before relying on that date.
